sections.name: File setup, acres, processor, fixture
sections.title: Setup for the in-memory demo data
sections.what: Loads the synthetic fixtures, the document processor, and helpers that build a parcel area value and process a fixture by its ID. These prepare the data the mock store uses.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the demo mode run without a database by building everything in memory.
sections.watch_out: The fixture helper uses a forced non-null lookup, so an unknown fixture ID crashes rather than returning a clear message.

sections.name: demoCase
sections.title: Builds one demo case
sections.what: Creates a full demo case with a location, a synthetic parcel, a synthetic family member, a progress count and starter documents. Progress shows 3 of 5 when documents exist and 1 of 5 when they do not. Two demo cases are built this way.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the screens realistic sample content to show without a live database.
sections.watch_out: A local value holding a fixture record is computed, but its use is not visible in the excerpt, so its purpose is unclear. The family member name uses the last three characters of the nickname.

sections.name: MockCaseRepository, mockCaseRepository
sections.title: In-memory case store
sections.what: Keeps demo cases in memory and provides actions to get a case, create a case with a timestamp ID, list fixtures, attach a fixture document, and process a document. Attaching adds a fixture only if no document of that kind exists yet. Processing marks the document as processing and then runs the processor on it.
sections.why: Likely reason: a stand-in for the real database so the demo runs with no setup.
sections.watch_out: The attach method is named attachFixture, but the CaseService interface names it attachDocumentFixture, so this class may not work where the interface is expected. All changes vanish on restart.

summary: In-memory stand-in for the case database that serves demo cases to the app.
purpose: Lets the app run its demo without a real database.
why: Likely reason: makes demo and development possible without any setup.
how: First, the file builds two demo cases from synthetic data. It keeps them in a lookup table keyed by case ID. Creating a case adds a new entry with a timestamp ID. Attaching a fixture adds one document per kind. Processing a document replaces it with the processed version.
inputs: Case IDs, nickname and location for new cases, fixture IDs for attaching documents, and document IDs for processing.
outputs: Case details, fixture lists, or null when a case or document is not found.
risks: All data is lost on restart. The attach method name differs from the interface name. Unknown fixture IDs cause a crash in the fixture helper. Stored objects are changed in place.
debug: If a demo case disappears, the server probably restarted. If attaching a document does nothing, a document of that kind may already exist. If a method is not found where the interface expects it, check the name difference.
